songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Other One jams and soaring Wharf Rat with crisp sound
ai_show_review.blurb: The August 15, 1971 show bursts into life with marathon The Other One explorations that showcase Phil’s front‑and‑center bass and Jerry’s fiery solos. A flowing Wharf Rat ties the second set together while Truckin' and China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider keep the momentum blazing. Pigpen adds a powerful vocal/harmonica lift, making this a standout early‑’70 performance.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Berkeley Community Theater on August 15, 1971 finds the Dead locked in high gear. The first set stumbles a bit with tuning woes but quickly finds its footing, delivering solid grooves on Cumberland Blues and a seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition that sets the tone for the night. The second set is where the show truly shines: Truckin' launches into an extended drum break before diving head‑first into back‑to‑back The Other One jams that let Phil’s bass roar and Jerry’s “Scurvy Les Paul” tone cut through with fierce, melodic leads. A second run of The Other One segues into a long, flowing Wharf Rat that feels both introspective and soaring, while Turn On Your Lovelight closes the set on an exuberant high note. Pigpen is in fine form, adding gritty harmonica and vocal fire that rounds out the band’s texture. Despite minor mix quirks—Jerry occasionally buried and Bob’s rhythm guitar disappearing for a spell—the soundboard captures the group’s chemistry with surprising clarity, making this a must‑listen snapshot of the early ’70 era.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with crisp overall mix and clear instrument separation; minor channel quirks do not detract from the high‑energy performance.

key_highlights: Marathon The Other One jams that highlight Phil’s front‑and‑center bass and Jerry’s soaring leads
A flowing Wharf Rat sequence that ties the second set together
Truckin' → Drums → The Other One chain delivers nonstop momentum
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition shines with tight interplay

band_performance.Jerry: Shows a fiery, "Scurvy Les Paul" tone and strong solo work throughout; occasional mix quirks make his guitar thin or buried in the left channel.
band_performance.Phil: Bass sits front‑and‑center, delivering excellent, melodic lines that drive the extended Other One jams.
band_performance.Bob: Rhythm guitar is solid overall but drops out at moments, reducing some of the usual rhythmic glue.
band_performance.Brent: Pigpen (Ron) is in good health, contributing powerful harmonica riffs and vocal energy that lift the set.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann provides a steady, propulsive foundation; his drumming underpins the high‑energy jams without any noticeable issues.
